# Show Card Position Outlines in HandView

## Problem Statement

Players have no visual indication of their hand capacity — they cannot see how many additional cards they can hold. Placing light card-position outlines in empty slots solves this.

## Users

- **Player** (Main Street, Golf, etc.) — sees empty hand slots as ghost outlines, knows instantly how many more cards they can buy/hold.
- **Developer** — enables outlines via a single boolean option on HandView construction; no scene-level wiring required.

## Acceptance Criteria

- HandView renders a semi-transparent card-sized rectangle at every position up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (ghost outlines behind real cards).
- Outlines are enabled via a new `HandViewOptions.showPositionOutlines: boolean` flag (default `false`).
- Outline rendering respects `reducedMotion` (no animation changes — outlines are static).
- Outlines update correctly on every hand mutation: `setCards()`, `addCard()`, `removeCard()`, `sortCards()` (animated path), and layout changes (`setSpacing()`, `setArcRadius()`, `setLayoutDirection()`, `setBaseX()`, `setBaseY()`).
- Outlines are destroyed on `HandView.destroy()` with no orphaned display objects.
- Unit tests verify outline creation, update, and destruction; a browser test in `GymHandPileScene` verifies visual correctness.

## Constraints

- **Visual style:** Stroke-only (no fill), 2px stroke width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, shape `CARD_W x CARD_H` rectangle centred on the card position.
- **When to show:** Always — outlines appear at every slot up to `maxSlots`, including occupied positions (rendered behind real cards).
- **API:** Two new `HandViewOptions` fields: `showPositionOutlines: boolean` (default `false`), `maxSlots: number` (optional — total slots to outline). If `maxSlots` is omitted and `showPositionOutlines` is `true`, outlines render one per current card (matching the occupied-position-only mode).
- **Depth:** Outlines render at depth `index - 0.5` so they sit **behind** card sprites (depth `index`) but above any background elements. If Phaser depth sorting proves unreliable, use a dedicated render group.
- **Layout direction:** Outlines must handle both `'horizontal'` and `'vertical'` layout directions.

## Existing State

- `HandView` (`src/ui/HandView.ts`) manages card sprite creation, layout (`layoutCardPositions`), selection, drag-and-drop, and event emission.
- No outline or ghost-rendering code exists in HandView or related UI modules.
- Game state already tracks hand capacity (e.g., `maxHandSize` in Main Street) — outlines would simply visualise the gap between current hand count and capacity.

## Desired Change

- Add `showPositionOutlines` and `maxSlots` to `HandViewOptions`.
- Add `private outlineRects: Phaser.GameObjects.Rectangle[]` field.
- In `rebuildDisplay()`, after creating card sprites, create outline rectangles for positions `0..maxSlots-1` (or `0..cards.length-1` if `maxSlots` is not set).
- In `applyLayout()`, reposition outline rectangles to match the new card positions.
- In `destroy()`, call `outlineRects.forEach(r => r.destroy())` and clear the array.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/HandView.ts` — Add `showPositionOutlines`, `maxSlots`, outline rendering, layout updates, destruction
- `src/ui/constants.ts` — No changes needed (uses existing `CARD_W`/`CARD_H`)
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymHandPileScene.ts` — Add a slider/button to toggle outline preview
- `tests/ui/HandView.outlines.test.ts` — Unit tests for outline lifecycle

## Related Work

- `CG-0MS937FT9006273E` — Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight renders over cards to the right (completed; depth ordering reference)
- `GymHandPileScene` — canonical Gym scene for HandView testing

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep:** Outlines are strictly visual — no click interaction, no animation. Animated entrance effects are a follow-up.
- **Assumption:** Phaser depth sorting at `index - 0.5` places outlines reliably behind card sprites. Verified against CG-0MS937FT9006273E pattern.
- **Vertical cascade:** Outline positions must cascade vertically matching card positions — layout code handles both directions.
- **Empty hand:** With 0 cards and `maxSlots=5`, 5 outlines render (useful for showing the full capacity of an empty hand).

## Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "What should the card-position outlines look like?" — Answer (producer): As proposed — stroke-only, 2px width, colour `0x666666` at `0.5` alpha, card-sized rectangles.
- Q: "When to show?" — Answer (producer): (A) Always — all positions including occupied ones, as ghost outlines behind existing cards.
- Q: "Configuration API?" — Answer (producer): "Whatever you think" → per-instance `HandViewOptions` boolean flag (default `false`).
data.title: Show an outline of card positions in the hand

# Intake Brief — Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end of turn cycle (CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q)

## Problem Statement

During the Main Street end-of-turn cycle, coins, reputation, and score are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` **immediately** inside `processEndOfTurn()` (via `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and `updateScore()`). The HUD display (`refreshHud()`) then reads these already-updated values and shows them instantly, while the end-of-turn animations (income collection, incident reveal) play afterwards. This creates a visual disconnect: the HUD shows new resource values before the coins fly from the card to the HUD display, and the game-over check (`checkEndConditions`) evaluates against the already-updated state before the player has seen the income feedback.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants resource changes to be visually synced: coins fly from cards to the HUD, *then* the HUD updates to reflect the new values. No premature game-over banners.
- **Main Street AI/headless sim players** — unaffected; the engine logic remains the same, only the presentation layer is affected.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I press "End Turn", I see the income coins animate from my producing business cards to the HUD display, and only after the animation completes do the coin/reputation numbers on the HUD update — so the visual feedback matches the state change.
- As a player, I should not see a game-over banner triggered by income that I haven't yet visually confirmed — the win/loss evaluation should happen after the final income animation lands.
- As a player, during the end-of-turn incident reveal, the coin/rep deltas from the incident should not appear on the HUD until the incident card's animation completes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Deferred state mutation:** `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, and any ongoing-cost deductions in `processEndOfTurn()` must **not** directly mutate `state.resourceBank` or `state.finalScore`. Instead, they compute deltas and return them in `TurnResult` as `pendingCoinDelta`, `pendingRepDelta`, and `pendingScoreDelta` (new fields).
- **AC2 — HUD persists pre-animation values:** During the end-of-turn animation window (`incomeCollectionActive` is true or an incident reveal animation is in flight), `refreshHud()` must display the **pre-animation** resource values (stored as `previousCoins` / `previousReputation`), not the mutated state values. The HUD only updates after the animation completes.
- **AC3 — State applied at animation end:** After the income collection animation (or incident reveal, whichever is last) completes, the pending deltas are applied to `state.resourceBank` and `state.finalScore` in a single step, followed by a final `refreshHud()` call. The `syncResourceBankToLedger()` is called after this final application.
- **AC4 — Game-over check deferred:** `checkEndConditions()` in `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` must NOT evaluate against post-animation state while animations are in flight. It should either: (a) run after the animation completes (recommended — restructure the closing flow so EndCheck runs after animation, or (b) accept the pending deltas as an optional parameter for the check.
- **AC5 — Reduced-motion mode:** When `reducedMotion` is true, there are no animations, so state is applied immediately as before (no regression). The deferred-path is only active when animations exist.
- **AC6 — Headless/AI sims unaffected:** `endTurnHeadless()` and the Monte Carlo harness continue to work without change — they bypass the presentation layer entirely. Engine logic (state mutations) still produces the same deterministic results; only the timing of HUD updates changes for the interactive path.
- **AC7 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
- **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The engine module (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) must remain deterministic and side-effect-free with respect to the HUD — engine mutations are for the AI/sim path only; presentation mutations happen in the scene/animator layer.
- `TurnResult` must carry all computed deltas so the scene layer can decide when to apply them.
- The `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` pattern (already used by `animateHudValueChanges`) should be extended to cover the end-of-turn window.
- No changes to game logic, economy calculations, or end conditions — purely a presentation/timing change.

## Existing State

- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `applyIncome(state)` which mutates `state.resourceBank.coins` and `state.resourceBank.reputation` directly (MainStreetAdjacency.ts:683, 707).
- **`MainStreetEngine.processEndOfTurn()`** calls `resolveIncident(state)` which also mutates `state.resourceBank` (MainStreetEngine.ts:~1720).
- **`MainStreetEngine.runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`** calls `updateScore(state)` which updates `state.finalScore` via `computeScore()` (MainStreetEngine.ts:1823).
- **`MainStreetRenderer.refreshHud()`** reads `s.state.resourceBank.coins` / `reputation` directly (MainStreetRenderer.ts:~398-400).
- **`MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`** calls `processEndOfTurn()` then `finishTurnPresentation(result)` which calls `refreshAll()` / `refreshAllExceptStreet()` immediately after.
- **`MainStreetAnimator.animateHudValueChanges()`** already tracks `s.previousCoins` / `s.previousReputation` and suppresses HUD delta pops when `incomeCollectionActive` is true, but the HUD text values themselves are already updated by `refreshHud()`.
- **`checkEndConditions()`** runs during `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` (before the next day starts) against the already-mutated state (MainStreetEngine.ts:1830).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()`, `applyIncome()`, `resolveIncident()`, `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()`, `TurnResult` type — defer mutations, surface deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — `applyIncome()` — compute deltas without mutating `state.resourceBank`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank`, `finalScore` — may need pending delta fields
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — `endTurn()`, `finishTurnPresentation()` — apply pending deltas after animations
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` — `refreshHud()` — display pre-animation values during animation window
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges()`, `animateIncomePhases()`, `animateIncomeCollection()`, `animateIncidentReveal()` — apply deltas on animation complete
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetScene.ts` — `previousCoins` / `previousReputation` tracking, `incomeCollectionActive` — extend to cover incident reveal too
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `checkEndConditions()` — defer or pass pending deltas
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — may need updates if commands mutate resources

## Related Work

- **CG-0MTV69NII000LW8I** — "Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card, growing right" (open, medium) — sibling presentation fix for the same end-of-turn income animation; the coin-grid anchor change is independent but should be merged close in time.
- **CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE** — "Animate end-of-turn income collection (coin fly-to-HUD)" (completed) — established the income collection animation that this task needs to respect.
- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** — "Incident reveal animation" (completed) — incident card flight + hold animation that also needs to respect deferred state.
- **CG-0MT5W7UJJ0065MEZ** — "In main street log should show total effects" (completed) — the per-turn net summary row; unaffected by this change.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** — "Phased income show (base → synergy → rep → events → upcoming → grid-to-HUD)" (completed) — the phased choreography that this task must gate state updates on.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep — re-architecting the engine:** The fix is presentation-layer only. Do NOT refactor `applyIncome`/`resolveIncident` to be purely functional (return-only) as that would break the headless sim contract. Engine mutations remain; the deferred-path applies them after animations.
- **Animation-completion callbacks:** Need a reliable mechanism to know when all end-of-turn animations have finished (income collection + incident reveal). The `incomeCollectionActive` flag plus a similar flag for incident reveal, or a single "closing animation active" flag with a completion callback chain, is the simplest approach.
- **Game-over timing edge case:** If the player reaches the score threshold during income, the game-over banner should only appear after the income animation completes, not before. This means `checkEndConditions()` may need to run after animation completes, which changes the current flow (currently runs before `startDayPhase()`). This is the correct behavior but needs careful restructure.
- **Undo/redo paths:** Undoing an end-of-turn action (if that were supported) would need to revert the pending deltas — but undo is cleared at end-of-turn anyway, so this is not a concern.
- **Assumption:** The engine (`MainStreetEngine.ts`) should still mutate `state.resourceBank` for the headless/AI path. The deferred mutation only applies to the interactive scene path. This keeps the engine module unchanged for non-interactive callers.

## Open Questions

- **Q1:** Should `checkEndConditions()` run (a) after animations complete and state is applied, or (b) immediately as it does now but using the pending deltas as a "what-if" evaluation? **Recommendation: (a)** — the game-over check should evaluate the final post-animation state, so the banner appears at the right visual moment. This means reordering `runSinglePlayerTurnClosing()` to defer EndCheck until after the animation window.
- **Q2:** The incident reveal animation (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I) also has resource deltas (`incidentCoinChange`, `incidentRepChange`) that mutate state. Should these also be deferred until after the incident reveal completes? **Recommendation: yes** — for consistency, all resource changes from the end-of-turn cycle should be deferred.

## Feature 1: Week-Window Data Model + CSV Schema

### Summary
Add optional `availableWeekStart` / `availableWeekEnd` CSV columns to card-data.csv, extend `EventCard` interface to carry these fields, and implement `isCardAvailableInWeek()` helper function.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `card-data.csv` has two new optional columns: `availableWeekStart` and `availableWeekEnd`.
2. `EventCard` gains optional `availableWeekStart?: number` and `availableWeekEnd?: number` fields.
3. `DurationEventCard` inherits these optional fields.
4. `MainStreetCards.ts` parses these columns — defaults to `undefined` when absent (year-round).
5. `isCardAvailableInWeek(card: EventCard, week: number): boolean` returns `true` when card has no window OR `week` is in range `[start, end]` inclusive.
6. Parsing is verified by a unit test that constructs a CSV string with window columns and asserts parsed cards carry correct values.

### Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Add new CSV columns
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — Extend EventCard interface and parsing; add `isCardAvailableInWeek()`
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetCards-week-window.test.ts` — Unit tests for parsing and helper

### Dependencies
None (foundational feature)
data.title: Add week-window CSV schema, parse into EventCard, and implement isCardAvailableInWeek helper

## Feature 2: Calendar State Model + Random Start Week

### Summary
Add `week` (1-52) and `year` (>=1) to `MainStreetState` and `MainStreetSerializedState`, initialise `week` at random from the allowed set `{1-8, 16-24, 40-46}` at game creation using the seeded RNG, and implement `advanceWeek()` helper that increments week (wraps 52-1) and increments year on wrap.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `MainStreetState` gains `week: number` (1-52) and `year: number` (>=1).
2. `MainStreetSerializedState` gains the same fields.
3. At setup (`setupMainStreetGame`), `week` is chosen uniformly from `{1-8, 16-24, 40-46}` using the game's seeded RNG.
4. Same seed produces the same start week (determinism unit test).
5. `advanceWeek(state)` increments `week` (wraps 52-1) and increments `year` on wrap.
6. `advanceWeek` is called at the end of each turn's day-transition (in `MainStreetEngine.ts` turn flow).
7. Unit tests cover: start-week determinism, `advanceWeek` wrapping at 52-1, year increment.

### Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` - Add week/year fields, random start, `advanceWeek()`, save/load
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` - Call `advanceWeek()` in turn flow
- `tests/main-street/CalendarState.test.ts` - Unit tests for calendar state

### Dependencies
- `CG-0MTTA6E4300699ZA` (Feature 1: week-window data model)

## Feature 3: Week-Gated Market Offers

### Summary
Gate `refillSingleRowMarket` investment offers on `isCardAvailableInWeek` — only Investment-trigger EventCards whose declared week window includes the current `state.week` are offered. Cards with no window remain year-round.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `refillSingleRowMarket` filters event cards (Investment trigger) through `isCardAvailableInWeek`.
2. Cards with no window remain year-round (offered every week).
3. Unit test forces `week=40` and shows Harvest Festival (weeks 38-41) becomes offerable while Summer Fest (weeks 23-35) does not.
4. Unit test forces `week=28` and shows Summer Fest becomes offerable while Harvest Festival does not.
5. Existing repeat-spacing and polarity constraints are preserved alongside week filtering.

### Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMarket.ts` - Gate `refillSingleRowMarket` on week window
- `tests/main-street/WeekGatedMarket.test.ts` - Unit tests for week-gated market offers

### Dependencies
- `CG-0MTTA6E4300699ZA` (Feature 1: `isCardAvailableInWeek` helper)
- `CG-0MTTA73RS007N566` (Feature 2: `week` field on state)

## Feature 4: Week-Gated Incident Draws

### Summary
Gate `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` incident selection on `isCardAvailableInWeek` — Incident-trigger cards whose window excludes the current `state.week` are skipped in addition to existing repeat-spacing / polarity constraints. Falls back to the nearest eligible card; if none eligible, the turn draws no incident (documented behaviour).

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` filters incident cards through `isCardAvailableInWeek` in addition to existing repeat-spacing / streak constraints.
2. Falls back to the nearest eligible card by the existing selection tiers.
3. If no incident card is eligible for the current week, the function returns -1 (draw no incident for that turn).
4. Unit test seeds an incident deck with a mix of year-round and windowed incidents and verifies window filtering at a specific week.

### Key Files
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` - Gate `findConstrainedIncidentIndex` on week window
- `tests/main-street/WeekGatedIncidents.test.ts` - Unit tests for week-gated incident draws

### Dependencies
- `CG-0MTTA6E4300699ZA` (Feature 1: `isCardAvailableInWeek` helper)
- `CG-0MTTA73RS007N566` (Feature 2: `week` field on state)

Producer feedback addressed and work pushed to dev (commit 4cf991bf).

Producer feedback (2026-09-19): outlines must match card position/rotation/spacing, must be visible in Main Street, Gym max hand size 7.

Changes:
1. HandView outline alignment (src/ui/HandView.ts): occupied outline slots now sit at the exact card rest positions and mirror the card sprite's ACTUAL rotation (custom-rendered cards that never rotate get straight outlines); extra capacity slots (maxSlots - hand size) continue the same spacing to the right and render below every card so they never draw over a card face; an empty hand renders all slots centred on the hand centre. Outlines respect reducedMotion (static). Capacity cap: outlines never exceed maxSlots even if the hand is transiently over capacity. New cardHeight HandViewOption for non-default card sizes.
2. Main Street (MainStreetRenderer.ts): showPositionOutlines: true, maxSlots = state.maxHandSize (synced on every refreshPlayerHand via setMaxSlots so staff-card capacity changes are tracked), cardWidth/cardHeight sized to the rendered hand card (handCardW-4 x handCardH-4). The producer's repro ('start a new game, outlines visible where the hand will be') is now covered: an empty hand shows 3 ghost slots.
3. Gym (GymHandPileScene.ts): explicit MAX_HAND_SIZE = 7 (maxSlots), drawToHand()/recallFromDiscard() refuse beyond capacity with illegal-move feedback; help text updated.
4. Tests: 8 new HandView outline unit tests (alignment, rotation mirror, extra-slot depth, capacity cap) — 31 total; Gym browser test updated to assert occupied slots align with cards (position+rotation) and extra slots sit below cards; NEW MainStreet browser test (tests/main-street/hand-outlines.browser.test.ts) verifies outlines enabled by default, count == maxHandSize, alignment with real cards, and pixel-visible rendering (ON vs OFF luminance delta > 45).
5. Docs: docs/DEVELOPER.md (Hand & Pile Rendering > Hand capacity outlines), docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md, AGENTS.md section 2.

Validation: full unit suite (365 files, 6519 tests) green; full suite (unit + browser + tutorial E2E) green at pushed commit 4cf991bf (0 failures); build green. Earlier full-suite Main Street browser failures were confirmed contention flakes (passed on re-run).

Intake questions (round 1/3):

1. **Stick figure appearance:** What should the stick figures look like? Simple line-art stick figures (head circle + body line + arms + legs), small coloured dots/circles, or something else? Should they match the Main Street art style?

2. **Walking behaviour:** Where exactly should stick figures walk on screen? Along the street strip below the business cards, wandering freely, or following a specific path?

3. **Figure-to-reputation ratio:** How many stick figures per reputation point? (e.g., 1 figure per 1 rep point, 1 per 5 points, capped at some maximum?)
